claims.statement: On the initial resume connection, `ServerReady` latches `_resuming` into `_restoring_resumed_history` before clearing connection state, keeping the status in resuming state through history restoration; reconnects do not re-arm that indicator or repeat initial session setup.

Static slash commands are declared once in `COMMANDS`; the registry derives queue-bypass sets including aliases and projects autocomplete entries, while experimental commands are omitted unless experimental mode is enabled.

After terminal server-start failure, `/install`, `/reload`, and `/update` can bypass the queue only while no agent, shell, or modal command is active; they otherwise retain their normal queued classification.

Interactive and headless clients start a temporary, ephemeral-port LangGraph runtime, wait for the `agent` graph, bind the resolved workspace, and clean up the server if startup fails or is cancelled before handoff.

The generated server checkpointer uses an ownership-fenced SQLite saver: a thread lease has an OS-lock-backed token, and every checkpoint mutation validates that token and live reservation so stale servers cannot write after client exit, release, or takeover.

The TUI serializes post-connect initialization as resumed-history restoration, optional startup command, initial prompt or skill, and queued user messages; `ServerReady` also installs server state and schedules deferred-action draining.

Headless execution is a single autonomous task whose shell policy defaults to shell disabled with other tools auto-approved; quiet mode reserves stdout for response text, and its documented exit codes include 124 for a turn budget and 130 for interruption.

Model retry wraps only the model node, avoiding replay of completed tool calls; it owns transient-error classification, backoff, and visible retry status, while the clients consume attempt and retry events to reconcile partial output.

Prompt-cache expiry is checked once per second: the TUI warns once in the final retention window, and when `warnings.cache_prompt` is `expiry` it offers a handoff only when idle; submitted interactive messages can hand off, send, or cancel while preserving the draft for handoff or cancellation.
`--acp` selects an ACP server over stdio instead of the Textual UI, while `--model-params` overrides configured model values and `--max-retries` overrides the configured retry count.

Thread names are validated as trimmed, printable single-line values of 1–50 characters and are stored independently of checkpoint revisions; thread listings prefer the durable saved name and fall back to latest root-checkpoint metadata.
The `/threads` selector can render cached rows before reloading disk state, supports a persisted cwd or all-directory scope, and treats changed durable names as a refresh-relevant difference.

Thread selection validates ownership before the modal dismisses; an ownership failure leaves the selector open, preserves its filter and selected row, and prevents history loading or active-thread replacement.

For most-recent resume, dcode attempts to lease candidates in recency order and skips occupied threads, but an explicitly selected occupied thread fails before history loading and preserves the current thread.

`@@` thread completion searches durable name together with thread ID, initial prompt, agent, branch, and cwd; it displays the saved name preferentially but inserts an ID-only `@@(thread:...)` reference token.

The local thread-inspector skill directs operators to a read-only script for trusted local session stores, warns against manual blob decoding and untrusted deserialization, and requires summaries to avoid unrelated secrets, personal data, and hidden reasoning.

`RemoteAgent` caches server-validated workspace descriptors per thread, requires an explicitly configured workspace before binding, and changes its active cwd and cache only after a workspace-switch request succeeds.

For a streamed execution, `make_graph` requires a nonempty thread ID and workspace context, verifies the durable workspace binding, and selects a workspace runtime keyed by binding identity and current runtime fingerprint; access-policy drift is rejected while runtime-only changes can rebuild the graph.

Server-owned context offload first idempotently registers the HTTP thread, transports workspace and ownership context, resumes hook interrupts using one operation ID, and on local cancellation waits for a terminal server acknowledgement before propagating cancellation.

Agent construction installs human approval only when neither automatic approval nor restrictive-shell headless handling disables it; an explicit filesystem tool allowlist is injected into synchronous subagents as well as the main agent to prevent delegated bypass.
